content.text:
I read every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a full limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure. Result: no untraced technical matter and no internal inconsistency found.

Key trace points:

- **Claims 1–17** — every limitation maps to an affirmative disclosure passage: three carriages, radial guides, pivoting concave pads "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter", segmented ring in an annular guide with one segment per half, complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by closure, followers in oblique slots, wedge on a ring drive face, limited stroke, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin vs. fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, carriage springs, the two latch positions, and the mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. Claim 6's "same inward travel" traces to "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" read with "rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others."
- **Numerals** — 28 entries, each with one meaning; 10/30 (whole) vs. 12/14, 32/34, 58 (parts) are consistently distinguished; every ledger numeral appears in at least one figure and in the description; every figure's front-matter list matches its placement targets and its trailing list.
- **Figure/description consistency** — hinge left / latch right (FIG. 1) is carried consistently into FIG. 3 and FIG. 6, so 44/48 land on the upper segment (32, carried by first frame half 12) at the hinge and latch junctions respectively, matching the description. FIG. 3's segment/junction layout and FIG. 6's enlargement agree, and 07-drawings agrees with all six briefs. No section lines are used, so no designation repetition is at issue.
- **Depiction conventions** — the FIG. 3 ring-drive-face placement rationale and the FIG. 1 mounting-boss placement are confined to the figure briefs, are stated as schematic, and expressly disclaim any circumferential or functional relationship; no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaked into the Field, Summary, Brief Description, or Detailed Description. FIG. 5's slot statement ("neither purely radial nor purely along the band") is the definition of the disclosed *oblique* slot, not an added angle.
- **No contamination** — the drafting agent's own conversation turn referencing a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" appears nowhere in the draft; no placeholders, open questions, or internal notes remain in the application text.

Flagging one thing outside my remit for your awareness, not as a finding: the brief states no prior-art search was run, so the Background's prior-art characterizations still need the separate `prior_art/` trace review.

content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all 17 claims (independent claims 1, 11 and 14 and dependent claims 2-10, 12-13, 15-17), every one of the 28 numbered parts in draft/numerals.md, every sentence of the field, summary, brief description of drawings, detailed description and abstract, and all six figure briefs back to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (the only inventor authority; the conversation contains one USER passage that is a truncated copy of the same text, and the "YOU" passage — which speaks of a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" — is context only and correctly does not appear anywhere in the draft). The disclosure supports: two semicircular frame halves, hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three radial jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave jaw pads and no tool-specific diameter; a segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half; complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by frame closure; a follower per carriage in a respective oblique slot; a latch-carried wedge bearing on a ring drive face and rotating the coupled ring through a limited stroke; synchronized inward carriage travel; outward carriage bias springs; first (holding) and second (over-center) latch positions; a force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing residual travel; a visible indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range that reports load and not diameter; the install and remove sequences; and an optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. Each of those maps to claim and description text without broadening. Internal-consistency checks passed: numerals are one-to-one with parts and every numeral in the table appears on at least one figure and in the description; part naming is uniform across claims, description, abstract and briefs ("ring drive face" 54 is kept distinct from the junction drive faces 44/46/48/50); the hinge-left/latch-right convention in FIG. 1 agrees with the left junction carrying hinge-end faces 44/46 and the right junction carrying latch-end faces 48/50 in FIG. 6, and the upper/lower assignment of frame halves 12/14 agrees with segments 32/34 in FIG. 3 and FIG. 6; the FIG. 3 conventional drive-face position is repeated identically in FIG. 6; no section lines are designated anywhere, so no section-designation mismatch exists; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. No "by way of example" or "any closed outline" style shape-justifying language leaked from a figure brief into the application text, and the FIG. 3 non-relationship disclaimer stays confined to the brief. The abstract is 146 words. One critical disclosure_fidelity defect remains: FIG. 5 verbalizes an undisclosed radial end position for the cam follower and an undisclosed axial layering of the cam ring band relative to the carriage, which is substantive functional-surface geometry rather than a depiction convention. I did not assess patentability, novelty, obviousness or prior art, and I did not inspect rendered images.

findings.title: FIG. 5 brief asserts an undisclosed radial end position for the follower and undisclosed axial layering of the cam ring over the carriage
findings.where: figures/FIG-5.md, "Geometry to draw" bullets 4 and 5 (follower and cam-ring band)
findings.detail: The FIG. 5 brief fixes where on the jaw carriage the cam follower sits and how the cam ring band is layered against the carriage. The follower is a functional cam element and the slot is a functional cam surface, so a statement of its radial end position on the carriage, and a statement that the ring band passes behind that end, convey technical substance about where the cam drive engages the carriage and about the axial stack-up of ring and carriage. The disclosure never locates the follower on the carriage and never gives any radial or axial relationship between the cam ring and the jaw carriage. The nearest source passages are "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring" and "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame" — both silent as to where on the carriage the follower is and where the ring lies relative to the carriage. There is no affirmative inventor passage placing the follower at the radially outer end or placing the ring behind the carriage. This is not curable by the schematic label: the guidance treats radial end positions and contact topology of a functional slot, cam or follower as substantive even when the brief calls the geometry schematic. The pad's inner-end position is different and is supported, because the disclosure states the pad "bears on a pipe" and the carriage travels inward, so that bullet may stand; likewise the outward spring direction is supported by "A spring biases each carriage outward" and may stand.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording (figures/FIG-5.md): "At the outer end of the carriage, which is the upper end, a follower drawn as a small circle." and "A portion of the cam ring is shown as a narrow arcuate band passing behind the outer end of the carriage. The follower lies on this band." Nearest inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring." No affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage of input/conversation.md states where on the carriage the follower is carried, or that the cam ring lies behind, in front of, or radially outward of the carriage.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-5.md replace the fourth bullet with: "- A follower drawn as a small circle carried by the carriage and spaced along the carriage from the pad." and replace the fifth bullet with: "- A portion of the cam ring is shown as a narrow arcuate band crossing the carriage at the follower, the follower lying on this band." Leave the pad bullet, the slot bullet and the spring bullet unchanged. No change is required to the claims, the description or the Brief Description of the Drawings, which are already neutral as to where the follower sits on the jaw carriage; do not add any compensating statement to the application text.
